chapter_plans.title: The Bell at 2:17
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Female Lead is awakened by the impossible ringing of the Saint Orison’s bell at 2:17 a.m., marking the start of a new death cycle in Morrow Wick.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Female Lead is jolted awake at 2:17 a.m. by the bell that should not exist. She tries to rationalize the event, but the community’s silent dread and the recent deaths make denial impossible. She connects the timing to the town’s infamous tragedies and her mother’s anxious warnings. Male Lead appears at the scene, deflecting questions and steering the investigation away from the town archives. Female Lead begins her own inquiry, noticing how the victims seem compelled to follow specific, repeated actions. The town’s fear intensifies as dawn approaches.
must_happen: Female Lead is roused from sleep by the bell, which rings at 2:17 a.m. despite having been removed decades ago.
Female Lead observes the immediate aftermath: neighbors emerging, a sense of ritual dread, and an unspoken expectation that someone will die before sunrise.
Female Lead notes her mother Ada Voss’s old warnings about the church and town secrets.
Male Lead arrives, officially taking charge but quietly steering Female Lead away from the municipal records and the church.
Female Lead witnesses the chosen victim compulsively reenacting the prior victim’s final actions.
Female Lead recognizes the repetition but cannot discern a deeper pattern.
must_not: Do not reveal the true mechanism behind the bell’s choice or the chain of testimony.
Do not state or imply that the deaths are anything but a mysterious curse or supernatural event.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "Who else heard it this time?" Female Lead snaps, before her feet touch the floor.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Female Lead finds a fresh name written in soot on her front steps just before sunrise.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: A faint, oily fingerprint—left on the window latch by someone who could not have reached it from the ground.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Rising dread, denial battling with logical curiosity, and the first glimmer of obsession.
chapter_plans.spice_note: No romantic or sexual content; tension is psychological and procedural.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Establish the impossible bell event, the cycle of ritual death, and the atmospheric dread of Morrow Wick in 1600–1900 words. Set up Female Lead’s practical skepticism and Male Lead’s secretive resistance. Do not reveal the truth behind the bell.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Female Lead is driven to investigate the official records and the church for explanations, setting the stage for further discoveries.

truth_background: [kernel.true_case] The deaths are not a random curse and the bell is not choosing sinners. The loop is an unfinished chain of testimony created by seven children who died beneath Saint Orison’s Church in 1974 and were erased from the town’s official records. Each victim is forced to carry one fragment of their final memory to the next person capable of exposing the truth. Elena is not the final sacrifice. She is the final witness.
[kernel.core_question] Can Elena break the cycle of ritual deaths and restore the erased names of the seven children before she becomes the final victim herself?

chapter_plans.title: Ash and Ledger
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Female Lead discovers a scorched 1974 attendance ledger with missing names and altered signatures, raising suspicions about the deaths’ connection to the church fire.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Compelled by the soot-written name, Female Lead begins combing the municipal archives and discovers the partially destroyed 1974 church attendance ledger. She notes the missing names and altered signatures, suspecting a link to the chain of deaths and the fire. Male Lead intercepts her, attempting to distract her with procedural tasks and casting doubt on her findings. Evidence surfaces that Ada Voss, her late mother, was anxious about the bell deaths and the church records’ integrity. Female Lead questions the randomness of the victim chain for the first time, but lacks proof.
must_happen: Female Lead investigates the archives and discovers the 1974 attendance ledger, scorched and with names missing.
Female Lead notices altered signatures and recurring inconsistencies in death records.
Clue C001 is planted: A particular alteration in the ledger points to an official signature pattern.
Male Lead redirects Female Lead, trying to prevent her from accessing the sealed records related to the church fire.
Female Lead finds evidence of Ada Voss’s anxiety about the bell deaths and the town’s official files.
Female Lead begins to question whether the chain of deaths is truly random.
must_not: Do not reveal the exact reason for the missing names or the nature of the attendance ledger’s importance.
Do not allow Female Lead to uncover the chamber beneath the church or the full scope of Ada Voss’s involvement.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "If you want the truth, you’ll need to burn your gloves," the archivist mutters as Female Lead enters the records room.
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: A second name appears overnight—again in soot, but written inside the church’s locked vestry.
chapter_plans.signature_detail_hint: The charred edge of the ledger curls around a pressed wildflower, perfectly preserved despite the fire.
chapter_plans.emotional_beat: Suspicion, refusal to accept coincidence, and the sting of personal betrayal by trusted authority.
chapter_plans.spice_note: No romantic or sexual content; psychological tension only.
chapter_plans.chapter_task: Introduce the archival investigation and the physical evidence (ledger, signatures, soot). Plant Clue C001. Build Female Lead’s suspicion about the chain’s randomness and hint at Ada Voss’s indirect involvement in 1600–1900 words.
chapter_plans.carries_to_next: Female Lead’s focus on the ledger and soot-written names will drive her to reexamine other town records and question the official narrative.

Male Lead confronts her inside the church, warning her to abandon the search and physically attempting to bar her from the archives. chapter_plans.beat_summary: At sunrise, Female Lead stands at the threshold of the sealed chamber beneath Saint Orison’s, the final key in her grasp. Inside, she discovers the skeletal remains of the seven forgotten children, the original attendance ledger, and Ada Voss’s correction page. The full truth crystallizes: Ada altered the record to ensure Female Lead became the final witness, not a victim. As Male Lead makes a last, violent attempt to stop her, Female Lead records every name, reading them aloud into the silence. The bell’s impossible tone splinters, then ceases. The evidence of the 1974 cover-up is undeniable, and the town’s cycle of ritual deaths ends. Male Lead is exposed and arrested, Ada Voss’s legacy is confronted, and the children’s names are restored at last.
